basis: A test's peak is its own process's peak resident memory (VmHWM; the process tree's PSS where it starts processes) when it runs alone in a fresh process, CPU, MiB, over every parameter; measured with scripts/measure_test_memory.py's plugin. The line is 2 GiB: CI's runner has 16 GB and four xdist workers, whole shards without a test over the line peaked at 8.2 to 9.8 GB across the five processes (measured on the default lane, 2026-11-01), and shard 3 with two of them at once (the arm battery, 8.3 GB, and the helix reference, 5.7 GB) at 14.4 GB, on a runner of 16 GB. A test over the line is marked memory_heavy and runs alone of its kind. The tests listed under the line were measured too, and are here to show how near it they come (the walks over every registry entry stay unmarked: marking a function marks every entry it walks). In the same whole-suite scan no other test grew its worker's resident memory by more than 1.45 GB. On 2026-11-02 the arm battery, which had been one test of 8.3 GB (the 8.1 GB of its worker's end in a single process, 541 s in a shard run), was split one check to a test and its worker was put under a ceiling of 1.5 GiB of resident memory (tests/_cache_ceiling.py): its tests peak at 1.8 GB or less in one process, measured on that file alone. Added 2026-11-02 (phase 7m-b's fix round, each alone in a fresh process, /usr/bin/time): the integrated wall image's oracle and its control at 3.0 GiB, marked; the near-wall run and the tube kernel's test at 1.43 GiB, under the line; re-measured on the capped image (the same way, each id alone) with the wall's table an argument of their programs, not a constant: the oracle's two ids and its controls at 1.5 GiB (3.2 GiB before), under the line and unmarked. Added 2026-11-04 (shard 3 of CI lost its runner at 97 % on a pull request, five times; the tests were measured each alone in a fresh process, /usr/bin/time, on a warm and on a cold compilation cache, the larger given): the hull contact's property tests, the frame property at 4.8 GiB (3.4 cold), the containment property at 2.5 GiB and the unchanged-where-free property at 2.4 GiB, marked; the stress draw's test at 1.8 GiB, under the line. These were not in the 2026-11-01 scan, which came before the contact's 0.2.0 to 0.4.0 tests. A peak alone does not show what ended the runner: the file's tests also leave their compiled programs in the worker, and on CI (sampled every 5 s) four workers held 15.5 GB of a 16 GB runner and all of its 3 GB swap at 97 %, which tests/oracles/test_hull_contact.py now answers by giving the programs back when a worker has grown 1 GiB (9.6 to 11.7 GB, no swap, on six runners of four kinds of processor). Added 2026-11-10 (W2a's fix round, each id alone in a fresh process, /usr/bin/time on a GitHub runner, its probe run 42837773932): the guard harness's reach test, which now steps the hand-over too, at 4.0 GiB with that point at blob 0.05, marked (the point is built at blob 0.25 since, its arrays smaller, the mark kept). Lubrication's gates (tests/oracles/test_lubrication.py), measured there too and marked on 2026-11-10 once the shard table dealt the file by test (so no shard holds more than one of the marked ids and they no longer queue on the lock together, which had run the shard holding the whole file past its 30 minutes): gate 4 at 2.6 GiB (its ellipsoid; its tube's 2.1 GiB), gate 8 at 4.4 GiB (the tube; the plane's 2.5 GiB), gate 8's controls at 2.8 GiB and gate 13 at 2.8 GiB. Their file gives JAX's programs back past 1 GiB of a worker's growth (tests/_cache_ceiling.py); without that four workers filled the runner and its 3 GB of swap and lost it (probe run 42828627965).
